title: Brace Expansion II
summary: For each lowercase letter x , the set of words it represents is \{x\} .
statement: For each lowercase letter x , the set of words it represents is \{x\} . For expressions enclosed in curly braces, the set of words is the union of the sets of words represented by each expression within the braces. For the concatenation of two expressions, the set of words is formed by concatenating each word from the first expression with each word from the second expression, resulting in a set of concatenated words. Given an expression, return a sorted list of the words it represents.
constraints: Expressions use union commas, implicit concatenation, braces, and lowercase letters.
hints: Recursive descent separates union at the current brace level from concatenation between adjacent factors.
Maintain a current product set and a union accumulator.
On comma merge current into union; on a factor take the Cartesian concatenation; on closing brace return their union.
These operations mirror the grammar precedence and sets remove duplicates.
editorial: These operations mirror the grammar precedence and sets remove duplicates.

tests.explanation: Concatenation with nested union yields ac,ad,ae,bc,bd,be.
Union removes duplicates and sorts to a,ab,ac,z.
